software_scope: Owned protocols00417/00418 only; full suite integration, rendering and publication checks owned by release lead.

findings.problem: Legacy count and febrile-neutropenia rules targeted the whole regimen and implied a mandatory 25% reduction, including cetuximab.
findings.resolution: Delay actions now target platinum and fluorouracil. The possible 25% reduction remains a Consultant decision after recovery. Severe prior cytopenia requires a separate history review.

findings.problem: The printed ANC bands overlap at 1.5. Artificial decimal cutoffs also left values between encoded bands.
findings.resolution: Continuous comparisons preserve the printed bands. ANC exactly 1.5 and fractional platelet counts above99 but below100 require source interpretation. Baseline eligibility remains separate.

findings.problem: Overlapping cisplatin renal categories could select a dose from the wrong band. Baseline exclusions and subsequent dosing were conflated. Hearing and neuropathy shared one grade.
findings.resolution: Exact CrCl distinguishes the baseline exclusion below60 from later 45–59 dosing at75%, below45 clinical review, and the fractional59–60 source gap. Peripheral neuropathy and hearing have separate actions.

findings.problem: Carboplatin lacked the20–30 extreme-caution range and the source renal-calculation safeguards.
findings.resolution: Added renal bands, absolute renal method, AUC5 confirmation, GFR cap125, creatinine freshness within48hours and the measured-GFR110% creatinine trend. The ratio is derived from entered serum values.

findings.problem: Fluorouracil liver equality boundaries, clinical hepatic severity and DPD/renal interpretation were incomplete.
findings.resolution: Values exactly85µmol/L bilirubin or180U/L AST require review. Hepatic category and severe renal reductions remain clinical decisions. Complete DPD deficiency is contraindicated; unknown or missing baseline results prevent starting. Partial deficiency is individualised and renal uracil results require caution.

findings.problem: Generic grade3 non-haematological and grade2 mucositis rules asserted automatic treatment holds not specified in these regimen tables.
findings.resolution: These inputs now request urgent clinical review without inventing a dose/recovery algorithm. The named drug-specific source actions remain available.
findings.source: Both NCCP documents, pp4–7; review pathways identified as implementation limits.

findings.problem: Suspected and confirmed interstitial lung disease shared a permanent-stop action. The first15minutes of the first infusion were not distinguished from later mild reactions.
findings.resolution: New respiratory symptoms hold cetuximab pending investigation; confirmed disease stops it. A first15-minute reaction stops the infusion. Later grade1/2 reactions have supervised slow-infusion actions and grade3/4 reactions permanently stop cetuximab. Prior stop history persists.

findings.problem: A generic severe-skin hold did not track recurrence, recovery or restart timing. Restart could restore a previously reduced dose.
findings.resolution: The source weekly restart doses250/200/150mg/m² require the episode number, recovery to grade2 or better within14days, prior dose and Consultant approval. Fourth events or failed recovery stop cetuximab. Intolerable toxicity, missing history, a lower prior dose or another active stop prevents an automatic numerical restart.
findings.source: NCCPp5Table3; EMA SmPC4.4p6; prior-dose guard explicitly identified as an implementation safeguard.

findings.problem: Schedule summaries implied automatic maintenance and omitted the different fluorouracil infusion options.
findings.resolution: Preserved00417 daily22hours versus00418 daily16–22hours and each alternative four-day infusion. The combination lasts up to6cycles. Maintenance needs a separate prescribed plan. Selecting maintenance excludes cytotoxic actions from this combination assessment and requests the correct cetuximab pathway.

findings.problem: NCCP permits ending observation after two uneventful infusions, while the current EMA SmPC requires at least one hour after every infusion. Indication wording also differs.
findings.resolution: Both source positions are recorded. There is no automatic early discharge or assumption of a curative platinum-combination pathway. A context-specific prescribing and consent review is required.

findings.problem: Drug interactions and baseline, during-treatment and post-treatment monitoring were incomplete.
findings.resolution: Added the DPD-inhibiting antiviral contraindication, warfarin/phenytoin monitoring, an urgent fluorouracil cardiac-symptom review and current monitoring. Electrolytes, magnesium and calcium continue monthly for two months after the last cetuximab dose.

findings.problem: The production dose-schedule renderer ignored prose administration notes, leaving both protocols without a displayed schedule.
findings.resolution: Added two explicit treatment_phases: combination cycle1 with400mg/m² cetuximab loading followed by250mg/m² on days8/15; combination cycles2–6 with250mg/m² on days1/8/15. Each phase includes source-specific platinum and daily fluorouracil rows. The alternative fluorouracil infusion is retained in its note and never becomes an extra dose. Maintenance remains a separate prescribed plan; no generic dose ladder was added. Clinical rules and patient profiles were unchanged.
